'''Tanguy Rivoal''' (born 1972)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.idref.fr/069852219|title = Rivoal, Tanguy (1972-....)}}</ref> is a French [[mathematician]] specializing in [[number theory]] and related fields. He is known for his work on [[transcendental numbers]], [[special functions]], and [[Diophantine approximation]]. He currently holds the position of ''[[:fr:Directeur de recherche au CNRS|Directeur de recherche]]'' (Research Director) at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS)]] and is affiliated with the [[Université Grenoble Alpes]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rivoal.perso.math.cnrs.fr/|title = Tanguy Rivoal - Directeur de recherche au CNRS|access-date=2024-11-19}}</ref>

== Education ==

Rivoal obtained his Ph.D. from the [[University of Caen Normandy|Université de Caen Normandie]] in 2001 under the supervision of [[Francesco Amoroso]]. His dissertation was titled ''Propriétés diophantiennes de la fonction zêta de Riemann aux entiers impairs'' (''Diophantine properties of the [[Riemann zeta function]] at odd integers'').<ref>{{Cite thesis|url=https://theses.hal.science/tel-00004519|title = HAL these - Propriétés diophantiennes de la fonction zêta de Riemann aux entiers impairs| date=29 June 2001 | publisher=Université de Caen | last1=Rivoal | first1=Tanguy }}</ref>

== Research ==

Rivoal's research focuses on several areas of mathematics, including [[Diophantine approximation]], [[Padé approximation]], arithmetic [[Gevrey series]], values of the [[Gamma function]], [[transcendental number theory]], and [[E-function]]. His notable contributions include the proof that there is at least one irrational number among nine numbers ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11), ..., ζ(21), where ζ is the [[Riemann zeta function]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=T. Rivoal |title=Irrationalité d'au moins un des neuf nombres ζ(5), ζ(7),…, ζ(21) |journal=[[Acta Arithmetica]] |year=2002 |volume=103 |issue=2 |pages=157–167 |doi=10.4064/aa103-2-5 |url=https://eudml.org/doc/277990|arxiv=math/0104221 }}</ref>

Together with [[Keith Martin Ball|Keith Ball]], Rivoal proved that an infinite number of values of ζ at odd integers are linearly independent over {{tmath|\Q}}, for which he was elected an Honorary Fellow of the [[G. H. Hardy|Hardy]]-[[Srinivasa Ramanujan|Ramanujan]] Society.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=K. Ball |author2=T. Rivoal |title=Irrationalité d'une infinité de valeurs de la fonction zêta aux entiers impairs |url=https://rdcu.be/d1Vol |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |year=2001 |volume=146 |issue=1 |pages=193–207 |doi=10.1007/s002220100168|bibcode=2001InMat.146..193B |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hrj.episciences.org/public/volumes/34/23Announcements.pdf|title = Announcements - Hardy-Ramanujan Journal}}</ref> They also proved that there exists an odd number ''j'' such that 1, ζ(3), and ζ(''j'') are linear independent over {{tmath|\Q}} where ''2 < j < 170'', a specific case of the more general folklore conjecture stating that {{pi}}, ζ(3), ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ..., are algebraically independent over {{tmath|\Q}}, which is a consequence of [[Grothendieck's period conjecture]] for mixed Tate [[Motive (algebraic geometry)|motives]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Stéphane Fischler |author2=Johannes Sprang |author3=[[Wadim Zudilin]] |title=Many odd zeta values are irrational |journal=[[Compositio Mathematica]] |year=2019 |volume=155 |issue=5 |pages=938–952 |doi=10.1112/S0010437X1900722X |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/compositio-mathematica/article/many-odd-zeta-values-are-irrational/3F6B80B30009E47D75716A96E618779D|arxiv=1803.08905 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=[[Jean-Benoît Bost]] |author2=François Charles |title=Some remarks concerning the Grothendieck period conjecture |journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]] |year=2016 |volume=2016 |issue=714 |pages=175–208 |doi=10.1515/crelle-2014-0025 |url=https://www.math.ens.psl.eu/~charles/crelle-periods.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author=[[:de:Joseph Ayoub|Joseph Ayoub]] |title=Periods and the conjectures of Grothendieck and Kontsevich-Zagier |journal=[[European Mathematical Society Newsletter]] |year=2014 |issue=91 |pages=12–18 |url=https://www.ems-ph.org/journals/newsletter/pdf/2014-03-91.pdf}}</ref>
